findings.where: Registered agent step, the "I'll serve as my own registered agent" card and its address tick
findings.reads: You must have a physical Florida street address and you'll sign the acceptance on the next screen.
findings.claims: A Florida street address is all an individual needs to serve as the agent; the tick at line 284 confirms only "I confirm this is my physical street address in Florida and not a P.O. Box."
findings.truth: s. 605.0113(1)(b)1: the registered agent must be "An individual who resides in this state and whose business address is identical to the address of the registered office". Nothing on the step asks or confirms Florida residency; stepValidation.ts:208-230 and server/validation.ts:223-232 check name, address, state FL and two ticks only.
findings.replacement: Card: "You must live in Florida and have a physical Florida street address; you'll sign the acceptance on the next screen." Tick (line 284): "I live in Florida, and this is my physical street address in Florida, not a P.O. Box."

findings.where: Registered agent step, the self-agent card on a conversion that keeps its agent
findings.reads: You must have a physical Florida street address and you'll sign the acceptance on the next screen. For an existing LLC, enter your agent's name and address exactly as the Division has them on file. This order does not change your agent.
findings.claims: The converting client will sign an acceptance on the next screen.
findings.truth: FloridaLLCFormationForm.tsx:296-298 hides the acceptance step for a conversion keeping its own agent, and stepValidation.ts:233-235 validates nothing there; no acceptance is signed.
findings.replacement: On a conversion: "Enter your agent's name and Florida street address exactly as the Division has them on file. This order does not change your agent, and there is nothing to sign."

findings.where: Registered agent step, the note under "Your registered agent will be"
findings.reads: Nothing to sign here — we execute the registered agent acceptance when we prepare your filing, and anything we receive for your LLC is posted to your client portal.
findings.claims: Everything received at the agent address is posted to the portal.
findings.truth: Terms 10(b): we post "service of process and official government correspondence"; Terms 10(c): "Packages and general mail may be refused, returned to sender, or destroyed. We have no obligation to forward anything received through unauthorized use of the address."
findings.replacement: Nothing to sign here — we execute the registered agent acceptance when we prepare your filing, and any legal process or official government correspondence we receive for your LLC is posted to your client portal.

findings.where: Certification & signature step, "Who is the authorized representative?"
findings.reads: For a company being formed, Florida defines it as a person authorized by a prospective member to form the company by executing and filing its articles of organization (§605.0102(8)(a)).
findings.claims: The italicized words are the statute's definition.

findings.replacement: For a company being formed, Florida defines it as "a person authorized by a prospective member of the limited liability company to form the company by executing and filing its articles of organization with the department" (§605.0102(8)(a)).

findings.where: Getting started step (and the site), the word "Converting"
findings.reads: Converting an existing Florida LLC
findings.claims: Adding protected series to an existing LLC is a conversion.
findings.truth: In chapter 605 "conversion" is the change of an entity's type (ss. 605.1041-605.1046; s. 605.0213(10) "certificate of conversion"); establishing a protected series is s. 605.2201, and the Intro tick (StepIntro.tsx:61) itself says the form "adds protected series to that company". The Terms never use "convert". The word is used site-wide (Pricing.tsx:55 "converting the Florida LLC you already have").
findings.replacement: Adding series to an existing Florida LLC (site-wide). Ruling needed.

findings.where: Series step, "How ownership works in this structure"
findings.reads: No series has its own separate owners, and ownership cannot differ from one series to the next.
findings.claims: Reads as a rule of law.
findings.truth: Florida's Act allows a protected series to have its own associated members: s. 605.2102(3) "'Associated member' means a member that meets the requirements of s. 605.2302." The single-ownership design is this product's choice, which the next sentence ("This is deliberate.") half-says.
findings.replacement: No series has its own separate owners, and in this structure ownership does not differ from one series to the next.

findings.where: Name check result, the "held" verdict line
findings.reads: Unavailable — this name belongs to a recently dissolved company, and Florida protects it for up to a year. Please choose a different name.
findings.claims: Florida protects a dissolved company's name for up to a year.
findings.truth: s. 605.0715(5): "The name of the dissolved limited liability company is not available for assumption or use by another business entity until 1 year after the effective date of dissolution" — that section governs administrative dissolution (605.0715(1)); the check applies 366 days to every inactive record (server/sunbiz.ts:160-165), whose comment attributes a 120-day voluntary-dissolution hold to "s. 605.0715(5)-(6)" that the text does not contain (read ss. 605.0714, 605.0715, 605.0716 in full). "Up to a year" is true of the administratively dissolved case; for other inactive records the sentence asserts a protection I could not find. Adam's rule (22 Aug 2026, sunbiz.ts:322-324) is that held blocks anyway.
findings.replacement: Unavailable — this name belongs to a company dissolved within the last year. Florida keeps an administratively dissolved company's name unavailable for one year (s. 605.0715(5)), and the state's records do not say which kind of dissolution this was, so we treat it as unavailable. Please choose a different name. Ruling needed on the 120-day claim in sunbiz.ts.
